quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
Riding conditions are normal.
The roadway is wet.
You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to let your legs absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: When you must ride over an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible. Keep the motorcycle upright and rise slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before hitting it, roll the throttle slightly to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: Which item will protect your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough eye protection.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider:

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intentions. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All the stopping power

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while riding:

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
There will be no change in steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Wearing a leather jacket.
Using the rear brake only.
Wearing goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect your face in a crash.
Is only useful for protecting against dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least one hour of riding.
After more than eight hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means the driver sees you.
Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Guarantees the driver will yield to you.
May make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to ensure a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass was started before the no passing zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within the posted speed limits and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps you:

options.text: Pass danger more quickly.
See less of the road so you can stay focused.
Have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
Follow the next vehicle's path more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of your lane.
Always stay away from the right side of your lane.
Always stay away from the center of your lane.
Use whichever lane position is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever lane position is safest.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road conditions. There is no single position you should always avoid.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Takes away your ability to steer.
Will usually correct itself.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to steer.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel and removes your steering ability. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Weave between the three parts of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver merge back too soon.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean as the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean as the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit forward without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop. Hand signals help riders communicate with each other.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to support your body rather than to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to support your weight. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep pace with that rider.
Split up so each rider can go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a set location later.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Speed up the engine.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to get off the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: Release the throttle and keep the bike straight as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Engine braking is:

options.text: Illegal.
Slowing down by turning off the engine.
Slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
Not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows the bike, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees the driver will yield to you.
Is not worth the effort.
Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will properly yield to you. Always stay alert.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Slam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and slam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together. Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal.
